title: SUE-T: Ethernet Transport for XPU Scale-Up Systems
short_description: Trace transactions, explain reliable delivery, and define accelerator completion contracts.
overview: Learn how SUE-T v1.0.0 carries accelerator memory transactions over an Ethernet scale-up fabric. Trace command mapping and acknowledgements, predict packet packing and recovery, map XPU and AXI interfaces, and compare completion points, memory visibility, and error handling. This intermediate technical course includes narrated slides, six synchronized teaching videos, worked examples, and knowledge checks. Allow about 75 minutes, including practice and review.

modules.summary: Endpoint scope, transaction flow, ACK modes, and visibility.

modules.summary: Queue service, packing limits, PDC state, and lossless reliability.

modules.title: Map the XPU Interface to the Transport
modules.summary: Command/network roles, identity, ordering, and encoding.

modules.summary: Visibility, errors, cleanup, and a worked AXI write.

long_description:
Learn how SUE-T v1.0.0 carries accelerator memory transactions over an Ethernet scale-up fabric. Trace command mapping and acknowledgements, predict packet packing and recovery, map XPU and AXI interfaces, and compare completion points, memory visibility, and error handling. This intermediate technical course includes narrated slides, six synchronized teaching videos, worked examples, and knowledge checks. Allow about 75 minutes, including practice and review.

**Overall duration: 75 minutes**

**Module 1: From XPU Transactions to Ethernet Transport — 18 minutes.**\
Endpoint scope, transaction flow, ACK modes, and visibility.

**Module 2: Efficient Packets on a Lossless Fabric — 25 minutes.**\
Queue service, packing limits, PDC state, and lossless reliability.

**Module 3: Map the XPU Interface to the Transport — 16 minutes.**\
Command/network roles, identity, ordering, and encoding.

**Module 4: Define Completion and Evaluate the Design — 16 minutes.**\
Visibility, errors, cleanup, and a worked AXI write.
